title: movsum
summary: Compute moving sums in MATLAB and RunMat.

gpu_support.notes: Real dense gpuArray inputs use provider-resident count-window reductions for scalar or [kb kf] windows, explicit dimensions, omit/include NaN modes, shrink/discard/fill endpoints, and sample/population normalization for movstd/movvar. SamplePoints and unsupported provider backends fall back to gather-once host evaluation and re-upload when an acceleration provider is active; complex GPU moving-window support remains tracked outside this resident real-dense fast path.

description: `movsum(A,k)` computes sums over a sliding window of length `k` along the first non-singleton dimension.
behaviors: `k` may be a positive scalar window length or a two-element `[kb kf]` backward/forward window.
Pass an explicit `dim` to move along a chosen dimension.
`'includenan'` is the default; `'omitnan'` and `'omitmissing'` skip NaN values inside each window.
`'Endpoints'` supports `'shrink'` (default), `'discard'`, `'fill'`, and numeric scalar fill values.
`'SamplePoints', sp` uses a strictly increasing numeric point vector for irregular moving windows. With sample points, RunMat currently supports shrink endpoints.
This implementation covers numeric, logical, complex, and gpuArray inputs; table/timetable `DataVariables` forms are tracked separately.
